area_summary: This slice is the operational heart of Strader: the corpus capture layer (Databento live streamer + T+1 pulls, GexBot 60s and 1 Hz collectors, Schwab stage snapshots, internals), its cron supervision mesh, and the preopen trading-day chain (Mancini parse, level tracker, premarket VP, heartbeat), plus the drill-bridge surface. Health is good where it matters most — every capture feed is cron-supervised on a */2 heartbeat with tests on the supervisor engine and key collectors — but the mesh concentrates risk in capture-supervisor-wrapper.sh (engine for all three supervisors) and in the Schwab refresh token, which three preopen jobs and two corpus feeds hang off with no offline fallback. The single most actionable gap is live-parity-wrapper.sh: the built-and-committed live-vs-replay integrity check for the capture path is waiting on one hand-installed cron line and has never run. Newest components (1 Hz orderflow leg, premarket VP, both 1-2 days old) and corpus_pull_internals carry no tests despite trading-day roles and, in internals' case, a prior silent-failure bug. Dead weight is clearly bounded: corpus_poll.py and corpus_pull_gexbot.py are superseded collectors that are actively dangerous to leave callable (double-writing the live corpus files), and _chain_es_backfill.sh, eod_view_schwab.py, es_volume_profile.py, and foundation09_paradox.py are finished-campaign leftovers safe to remove.

area_summary: This slice holds the back half of Strader's scripts/ tree: the measurement-study family, the orderflow watch/drill/edge-test cluster, the Schwab token lifeline, and the replay-drill workflow. Health is bimodal — the cron- and skill-wired core (mi_gauge, premarket VP, token refresh/health, surface_liveness, replay/drill family, parity protocol) is tested and actively maintained, while roughly half the files are completed one-shot studies that delivered their findings and now sit unwired as reproducibility artifacts. The biggest risks are trading-day-critical unsupervised processes and single points of failure: orderflow_sentinel runs live with no cron supervisor (a crash is silent until a human notices), refresh_schwab_token was fixed for reporting success on a defective grant only today, run.sh is an untested May-era gate every Schwab operation funnels through, and surface_liveness must manually track each new watcher or tap-in goes blind to it. A canonical-watcher ruling is also overdue — orderflow_monitor (journaling, not running) versus orderflow_sentinel (running, alerting) overlap with no stated verdict, and the residual_gate audit prescription is imported by nothing, so it enforces nothing. Dead weight: the Excel pair (poll_to_excel, stream_to_excel), probe_databento_live, and validation_batch_st3vu (which retains a metered-spend path) are clear deletion candidates, and several May-era study scripts carry frozen day-lists or stale frozen inputs that would mislead if rerun today.

area_summary: Strader/market is the typed core of the trading stack: corpus collectors (Schwab/GexBot/Databento pulls feeding data/corpus/), the orderflow footprint pipeline (bars → engine → imbalance → recognizer → profile, held deterministic by a CI parity snapshot), market-internals gauge, TPO/volume-profile analytics, and measurement study cores for flies and the leg profiler. Health is good at the center — the orderflow and corpus paths are cron/supervisor-wired, well-tested, and actively committed through 2026-08-11, with live==replay now measured (run_log, 08-09) rather than assumed. Biggest risks: corpus/paths.py and corpus/writer.py are single points of failure for irreplaceable tape yet writer and gexbot_stream have no direct unit tests; calibration constants (internals_config, orderflow_config, MIGauge scales) are frozen seeds with no recalibration cadence; and gex_context runs on ~days of GEX history. One notable gap: orderflow/regime.py — the flush-alert regime read Steve personally drove on 08-05 — is built and tested but wired into no live surface. Dead weight is the May-17 entity-model stratum (resolve.py, position.py, spread.py, chain.py, gex_profile.py, indicators/gex+gex_calc+registry, ingest/schwab+gexbot+mancini): a parallel typed-ingest architecture the corpus/orderflow design superseded, now kept alive only by its own tests and the strader.feeds catalog, and dangerous mainly as duplicate GEX/Schwab/Mancini paths that could silently disagree with the live ones.

area_summary: Strader/core-libs is the shared library tier: the gated Schwab broker wrapper (broker_schwab), the strader package (config/settings, token and capture-health assessors, market calendar, alerts, entities/evaluate/execution), the present formatting layer, session daemons, and dev QA tools. Health is bimodal — the credential/collector spine (settings, schwab_token, market_calendar, capture_health, alerts) is current, well-tested, cron-wired, and trading-day-critical, while a second stratum (playbook/evaluate entities, strader.feeds seam, present regime/signals) is tested-but-unwired scaffolding from May-July that nothing calls. Biggest risks: the alert push path has no self-test, the hand-maintained holiday tables age out, the May-frozen mock client drifts from the evolving real client, and the strader.feeds seam is bypassed by every actual consumer so its catalog rots unenforced. Dead weight is concentrated and clear: all three daemon/*.sh scripts are March-era domain-factory artifacts depending on a nonexistent /usr/local/bin/zgent-invoke and a gtuser tmux layout that predates the moocity socket, and present/driver.sh invokes a present.cli module that does not exist. The FD0 execution package (Aug 2026) is the one active-dev front — fully tested, never-transmit by construction, awaiting its runtime wiring.

area_summary: This area is the Mancini letter machinery: the live v2 pipeline under runbook/mancini (blob fetch → clean → in-session prompt extraction → validate → desk publish + Pine/payload emit + level-state tracker), plus the datastream gate, pre-open heartbeat, and risk-state reset under runbook/, and a legacy top-level mancini/ package from May. Health of the live pipeline is good: every runbook module is wired to the 08:15/08:20/08:25 crons or the /mancini-parse skill, has a dedicated test, and carries commits through 2026-08-11/12. Biggest risks are the trading-day-critical single points: run.py hardcodes two cross-repo COO desk paths, fetch.py leans on the external Azure CLI, validate.py is the sole guard against a hallucinated LLM level reaching Steve's chart, and risk_state's HALTED trigger depends on manual P&L recording. The top-level mancini/ tree is two-thirds superseded: parser.py and pine_emitter.py survive as live libraries imported by runbook/mancini/chart.py, but codegen.py and its five satellites (compositor, gallery, persist, post_mortem, replay) are dead-candidates with no invocation outside May archives and COO specs — folding the two live modules into runbook/mancini would let the whole legacy tree be deleted. The dead replay.py also name-collides with the active orderflow replay system, which is grep-noise worth removing.

The biggest structural risk is that nothing automated runs the suite: no cron, hook, or CI invokes pytest, so it only executes when an agent remembers the quality-gate step, meaning trading-day-critical paths (datastream gate, heartbeat, Schwab token refresh, GexBot collect window, Mancini parse) are guarded only by discipline. Secondary risks: GEX indicator tests frozen at May 17 while GexBot went live in August, the live-parity wrapper exists in scripts/cron/ but is absent from the active crontab, the conftest surface list must be manually extended for each new live surface, and the two lexicon xfails depend on st-g9y rulings that may never land. Dead weight is essentially zero — this area is the healthiest kind of accumulation, though the May-vintage COO-authored entity/present tests deserve a drift check against the newer desk pipeline.

area_summary: COO/factory is the enterprise's ops backbone: WSL image build/repave pipeline, post-build provisioning, zgent hydration and certification tooling, the automated test harness, and — most consequentially — the scheduled durability jobs (beads remote push/restore drill, Claude Monitor backup, boot-event recorder, binfmt guard) plus two cron wrappers, one of which (corpus-daily-wrapper.sh) is trading-day-critical because it is the entry point for Strader's datastream gate. Health is two-tier: the August-maintained durability scripts and cron wrappers are in good shape with heartbeats and some tests, while the April-era image/post-build chain is active but stale, risking drift against the parts that moved in July (post-build.sh vs verify.sh/clone-repos.sh, delta-apply vs full build, validate-runtime dropped from the pipeline). Biggest risks: COO still "temporarily" owns Strader's corpus cron with hardcoded cross-repo paths and no handback; check-dolt-schema-skew.sh lost its only invoker when Gas City was suspended, so nightly beads pushes run without the schema preflight; and harness self-tests plus most factory scripts have no automated runner, so regressions surface only at repave time. Dead weight is concentrated and easy to cut: the entire mempalace spike (hooks unwired from every settings.json, installer orphaned), apply-superpowers.sh, the manifest pair, pipe_pane_log.sh, wait_for_text.sh, backfill-propernames.sh, and three overlapping hydrate/rehydrate-moocity scripts that should collapse into hydrate-zepo.sh. Files directly serving Strader: corpus-daily-wrapper.sh (datastream gate), strader-reauth.sh (Schwab re-auth surfacing), hydrate-zepo.sh + session-start.sh template + the certification checkers (Strader's config and pending Zgent certification flow).

area_summary: tmuxMOO is COO's tmux presentation layer: the machinery that builds Steve's desk session and renders every Steve-facing document to /var/moo/desk — the daily delivery surface for Mancini parses, premarket VP pages, and trading-desk refreshes. Dead weight dominates by count: roughly 40 of 60 files are Gas City-era gc-root machinery (dashboard, desk-materialize/reset/shell, canvas scripts, navigator, vscode bridge/monitor, plan tooling, exec.sh, unused log-rotate and hourly-summary crons) with no live wiring, plus duplicates of surface-publish and surface.py that drifted from the zgent-subsystems copies. area_summary: This area is two generations of COO infrastructure: myDesk (the March/April XState operator-desk experiment plus a small live trading-delivery shim) and zgent-subsystems (the April 8 Gas Town import of mail/presence/health/lifecycle machinery). Health is bimodal — exactly three files carry live weight: trading-desk-refresh.sh (invoked every trading morning by Strader's Mancini runbook and therefore trading-day-critical), render-md.py (convention-mandated desk renderer, touched Aug 3), and plan-evaluate.js (Anthropic-API CLI fixed Aug 9 but with no discoverable wiring); everything else — the entire desk.js/hub/machines stack, all 27 zgent-subsystems files, and 11 myDesk tests — is dormant or dead, untouched since April–May. The biggest risks are: trading-desk-refresh.sh's documented silent-skip of the browser re-render under cron (the exact stale-Mancini-page failure Steve already hit), zgent-subsystems/lib/common.sh being gitignored and untracked (the subsystem's shared library exists only on this box), and two designed-but-never-wired maintenance loops (patrol.sh's 30s health cron and log-reap.sh, with /var/moo/logs growing unbounded as evidence). Dead weight is substantial and safe to name: backfill-questions.js and attention-loop.js (myDesk), render-md-pane.sh, and otel-env.sh have zero live references, and the whole desk.js stack still targets a deprecated 'gc-root' Gas City session that no longer exists. A catalog/test plan should protect the three live files first and treat both dormant trees as archive-or-delete decisions rather than test targets.

area_summary: COO/tests is a small, well-written bash unit-test suite (9 files, all with mocked/scratch state, safe to run) but it is entirely orphaned from automation: there is no runner script, no CI, no cron hook — the only wiring in the whole directory is one CLAUDE.md line telling agents to run test-zepo-heartbeat.sh manually, so nothing detects when these tests break or when their subjects drift. Coverage is concentrated on two slices — the pulse-zepos skill libs (5 tests, though zepo-fetch.sh itself is untested) and three of ~21 factory/scripts (record-boot-event, check-dolt-schema-skew, install-bd) — leaving essentially all other COO areas at ZERO tests from this directory: ecc/materializer (21 files), tmuxMOOOL... tmuxMOO (~50 files), .claude/hooks (23 files, only the PULSE_RUN bypass of session-start.sh covered), the remaining 18 factory/scripts (beads-remote-push, beads-restore-drill, backup scripts — all cron-live and untested), tools/okf, myDesk machines, and factory/mempalace; other test dirs exist elsewhere (factory/harness/tests, zgent-subsystems/tests, myDesk/test) but were outside this area. Biggest risks: the dolt-schema-skew test's sole fixture is the PaneWarden v54 backup at /var/moo/backups/beads-stores/ (verified present) whose deletion silently converts the suite to green skips; and the three zepo tests frozen since 2026-05-07 may assert behavior the libs have since outgrown. No dead weight — every test's subject is live, most via the nightly 22:30 pulse cron — the problem is invisibility, not rot. Cheapest high-value fix for the review plan: a tests/run-all.sh wired into COO's session or pulse cadence.
